title: The catering problem
narration: Stage One reaches four and eight hours. Our extension plans catering production: batch quantities and shared allocations, cookers and qualified workers, and preparation, cooking, packing and cleaning. Departures, freshness and resource calendars constrain the plan. Urgent orders and outages trigger replanning while started work stays fixed. We minimize missed meals, waste, batches and changes.

title: Complete meals and food waste
narration: For a meal lot, binary main coverage times side coverage gives complete service. Their sum minus twice their product counts unpaired components. Coverage is linear in batch-selection bits, so both expressions remain quadratic without auxiliary product bits. We prioritize missed meals, waste, batches and plan changes. Integer bounds prove that ordering and the hard-constraint penalty.

live_narration: Main coverage times side coverage gives complete service. Their sum minus twice the product counts unpaired food. Both expand quadratically without product bits. We prove the objective priority order and a penalty bound that makes every ground state feasible.

narration: We selected the QAOA configuration on the cell and S0/S1. On held-out S2/S3, it finds the offered-pool optimum in all ten seeds at both budgets. At two hundred fifty-six evaluations, median optimum probability per shot is about eleven and twenty-two times random-angle search. Angles are optimized per instance. These restricted portfolios still exclude better full-grid schedules.

title: VQE concentrates more probability on the optimum
kicker: SECOND QUANTUM METHOD · DIFFERENT COMPUTE BUDGET
narration: VQE uses one-hot Givens gates and controlled rotations between coupled blocks. With exact CVaR and adjoint gradients, median optimum probability is about twelve percent on both held-out cases. That exceeds our QAOA probability, but parameter counts, training budgets and final shots differ. The primary VQE setup hits ten of ten and nine of ten seeds.

title: VeloxQ: better plans after idle elimination
kicker: SAME FEASIBLE SCHEDULES · DIFFERENT SEARCH LANDSCAPE
narration: VeloxQ solves the larger kitchen. Removing redundant idle bits preserves feasible schedules and their objective. At equal twenty-thousand-step budgets, the best checked plan serves fifty meals instead of ten, out of one hundred forty. Waste rises from thirty to sixty portions: complete service has priority. Valid returns rise from seventeen to all five hundred twelve. This is one exploratory job per representation; classical controls still find better plans.

live_narration: For VeloxQ, proved idle elimination improves the best plan from ten to fifty meals served at the same step budget. Waste increases; our objective prioritizes service. Valid returns rise from seventeen to five hundred twelve. Classical controls still find better plans.

title: What scales, and where each method fits
narration: More orders and time choices create more programs and conflicts. QAOA uses thirty-one to thirty-five qubits in explicitly restricted portfolios. VeloxQ runs the larger coupled matrices. Classical references measure quality and representation loss. Variable count alone does not prove classical hardness or quantum advantage.
live_narration: Orders, time choices and conflicts drive scale. Quantum circuits use small portfolios; VeloxQ handles larger matrices. Size alone does not establish hardness.
